text:
maya: quick RFC follow-up — proposal to refactor the tenant throttle registry into a sharded handoff coordinator. goal: keep the fast path local (low-latency token buckets) while centralizing long-term fairness and abuse signals. sketching tradeoffs and migration steps.

jonah: curious — why hand-off instead of keeping a fast central cache with sticky routing? what's the failure model?

maya: main reason is hot-tenant tails. sticky routing plus central cache still costs an RPC on cold routes and amplifies load concentration. handoff = short TTL leases so local buckets can serve bursts without hitting central on every request. failure: if coordinator unavailable, local buckets either run degraded (serve from last lease) or fallback to global admission. tradeoff: increased complexity around lease reconciliation.

selena: how do we preserve cross-tenant fairness? if locals run independently we risk short-term unfair bursts that skew metrics.

maya: plan: two-tier approach — local buckets for micro-burst latency (tens to hundreds ms), global coordinator enforces longer window fairness (seconds to minutes). coordinator periodically recomputes global weights and issues corrective throttles or probation flags.

arjun: abuse detection question — if an attacker wheels lots of short-lived clients, they could get many local leases across shards. can coordinator revoke quickly?

maya: yes — coordinator can push immediate overrides. design includes an "override" channel where coordinator broadcasts revoke/limit commands per tenant+shard, with high priority. also probation flags that ripple into routing (move tenant to stricter backends).

liam: ops/migration: how to rollout without blasting production? any canary plan?

maya: proposed rollout: 1) passive mode — coordinator watches and writes suggested leases but local services ignore them (read-only). 2) opt-in shards — enable handoff for low-impact shards/regions. 3) canary tenants with traffic mirroring. 4) global enable. each step emits reconciliation metrics.

maya: example of a simple lease config (pseudo-yaml):
```
shard: s-15
tenant: acme-prod
lease_ttl_ms: 1500
tokens_per_lease: 1200
reconcile_interval_ms: 5000
priority: normal
```

selena: a couple practical asks: idempotent handoff (retries should be safe), opaque lease IDs with monotonic counters, and a backoff window if coordinator is flapping. also add a metric for "stale-lease-serves".

maya: agree — will add idempotency and a small jittered backoff for lease acquisition. will add stale-lease-serves, handoff_success_rate, handoff_latency.

infra-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4573 — adds sharded coordinator prototype + sim harness :robot_face:

arjun: one more ops concern — telemetry volume. frequent lease renewals could spike control plane. maybe use adaptive renew: longer TTL for stable tenants, short for spiky ones.

maya: good call. we'll compute TTL from recent variance and use adaptive windows.

liam: can we get eng-sre to run chaos tests (coordinator partitions) before canary? @eng-sre

jonah: adding to next platform sync agenda, and i'll ping eng-sre. ack on the plan.

maya: thanks all — i'll update the RFC with the handoff diagram, reconciliation seq, and rollout playbook, and follow up with the sim results from PR 4573.
